# Repository metadata

GitHub's own metadata is not stored in the repo, so it lives here as the source of
truth. Apply it under **Settings → General** and the **About** panel on the repo home
page. Description and topics are what GitHub search ranks on alongside the README, and
the description doubles as the meta description Google shows.

## About → Description

Keep it under 350 characters and lead with the phrases people actually search.

```
Free Elementor Pro add-on that renders one Loop Grid per taxonomy term — group posts by category, tag, brand or any custom taxonomy, each with its own heading, from a single widget. Works with custom post types and WooCommerce product categories.
```

## About → Website

```
https://beenacle.com
```

## About → Topics

GitHub allows up to 20. These are ordered by value: the first block is what people
browse, the second is long-tail intent.

```
elementor
elementor-pro
elementor-addon
elementor-widget
elementor-plugin
elementor-page-builder
wordpress
wordpress-plugin
loop-grid
loop-builder
taxonomy
custom-post-type
woocommerce
post-grid
categories
php
```

## About → checkboxes

* Releases — **on** (the in-plugin updater installs from GitHub Releases).
* Packages — off.
* Deployments — off.

## Social preview image

Upload `assets/icon-256x256.png` on a plain background, or a 1280×640 card reading
"Elementor Taxonomy Loop — one Loop Grid per taxonomy term". This is what shows when
the repo is shared on social platforms and in some search results.

## Why these choices

* `elementor-addon`, `elementor-widget` and `elementor-plugin` are the three topic pages
  Elementor add-ons are actually browsed under; being on all three widens the funnel.
* `loop-grid` and `loop-builder` are low-competition but exactly what someone hunting
  this capability types.
* `woocommerce` and `custom-post-type` capture the two largest non-blog use cases.
